title: Why Not Me
description:
The promotion list came out.
{name}'s name wasn't on it. A junior hire who joined last year got promoted first.
The direct manager said, "Not many spots this cycle — I'll make sure to take care of you next year."

{name} has heard that line twice before.

choices.text: Manage the expression. Keep going quietly.  (endurance / self-esteem drain)
choices.result_text:
{name} stayed late that night.
Still believed the work would eventually speak for itself.

choices.text: Request a one-on-one. Ask for the criteria.  (agency / friction risk)
choices.result_text:
Manager said, "Your performance was strong — it's a shame."
Never named the criteria.
{name} understood then: the process was opaque by design.

choices.text: Start looking elsewhere. Quietly.  (exit strategy / uncertainty)
choices.result_text:
{name} pulled out the résumé that evening.
More resolution than anger — this place is not the only place.

title: Founding Member
description:
College classmate Jaehyun tracked {name} down.
"I'm building something and need one more co-founder. You're exactly who I want."
10% equity, stock options, modest salary for now.

Jaehyun has conviction. The idea isn't bad.
But success rates aren't written anywhere.

choices.text: Join. Opportunities need to be taken.  (bet / uncertainty)
choices.result_text:
{name} said yes.
Small office, small team, large ambition.
Might not work — but this choice felt right.

choices.text: Decline. Need to build my own foundation first.  (stability / path not taken)
choices.result_text:
Jaehyun was disappointed but understood. "Any time you change your mind."
{name} kept walking their own road.
How Jaehyun's startup turns out — will be known later.

choices.text: Offer to advise. Can't join, but won't leave.  (compromise / connection)
choices.result_text:
{name} took a part-time advisory role.
Energy divided — but neither door closed.

title: LinkedIn Message
description:
A message arrived on LinkedIn.
"I came across your profile and believe you'd be an excellent fit for a current opening."

Benefits look good. Salary 15% above current.
Present job is familiar — that one is unknown.

choices.text: Set up a meeting. At least hear them out.  (information / focus split)
choices.result_text:
Met the HR contact at a café.
Actually not bad terms. Whether to move — still unclear.
But {name} learned something: what the market thinks this experience is worth.

choices.text: Politely decline. Current role is the right fit.  (stability / path closed)
choices.result_text:
"Appreciate the outreach, but I'm staying put for now."
Focused on the present role.

title: A Number Seen by Accident
description:
A colleague's pay stub opened on the wrong screen during work.
Same tenure. Same title.
₩2,000,000 more than {name}.

They pull the same hours. Same overtime.
The number, seen by accident, refuses to leave.

choices.text: Forget it. Act like it wasn't seen.  (peace / self-esteem cost)
choices.result_text:
{name} closed the screen.
Tried to forget. Couldn't quite.
The commute home felt longer.

choices.text: Request a formal salary review.  (agency / risk)
choices.result_text:
{name} filed for an HR meeting.
"I'd like to discuss a compensation adjustment."
Results in a month — the wait was difficult.

choices.text: Ask the colleague quietly.  (information / awkwardness risk)
choices.result_text:
The colleague was awkward at first — then opened up.
Negotiated harder at hire.
{name} hadn't known that one conversation could set a gap that follows for years.

title: Meaning vs. Money
description:
An environmental NGO reached out.
Must have seen the volunteer work — there's a full-time offer.
30% lower salary than now.
But the work would connect to something real.

Gangnam gets farther. Meaning gets closer.

choices.text: Take it. Money isn't everything.  (meaning / goal deferred)
choices.result_text:
{name} joined.
Money was tight. But Monday mornings felt different — wanted to get up.

choices.text: Decline. The goal comes first.  (goal / meaning set aside)
choices.result_text:
Politely declined.
Whether it was right — that answer comes later.

choices.text: Volunteer on weekends. Keep both.  (balance / energy divided)
choices.result_text:
Weekends for the cause, weekdays for the goal.
Divided energy — but nothing had to be surrendered.

title: First Commission
description:
Someone saw the work posted on social media and reached out.
"Could you do something similar for me? Budget is around ₩300,000."

First time. No contract framework, no clear process.
But every first job is somebody's first job.

choices.text: Take it. Learn while doing.  (leap / uncertainty)
choices.result_text:
A week of work. Three rounds of revisions.
When ₩300,000 landed — the most satisfying money earned so far.

choices.text: Wait until more prepared.  (perfectionism / opportunity lost)
choices.result_text:
"I'll reach out when I'm more ready."
The client moved on.
The definition of 'ready' — {name} still isn't sure.

title: Which Side
description:
An invisible line has appeared in the team.
Team Lead A's camp vs. Senior Manager B's camp.
Separate lunches, separate positions.

Both have texted {name} to join them for lunch.
Where you sit may determine next month's performance review.

choices.text: Go with the team lead. Follow the hierarchy.  (stability / suppressed opinion)
choices.result_text:
{name} sat with the team lead's side.
The senior manager's expression was neutral — but noted.
Choosing a direction in an organization closes the other ones.

choices.text: Go with the senior manager. Follow the competent one.  (principle / friction with leadership)
choices.result_text:
{name} sat with the senior manager's group.
The manager appreciated it. The team lead turned a few degrees colder the next day.
Doing the right thing isn't always the strategically safe thing.

choices.text: Skip both. Eat alone.  (independence / isolation)
choices.result_text:
"Something came up" — and ate at the convenience store alone.
Got a little colder from both sides.
But peaceful.

title: Just One More Day
description:
On the subway home.
Three times today. Swallowed it three times.
The manager's comment, the pointless overtime, the work nobody noticed.

"What if I just sent a text tomorrow and didn't show up?"
This isn't the first time that thought has appeared.

choices.text: Just endure it. No impulsive moves.  (patience / burnout)
choices.result_text:
Went in the next morning.
Nothing changed. Another day passed.

choices.text: Start planning an exit. Emotion first, strategy second.  (planned exit / double load)
choices.result_text:
{name} pulled out the résumé. Today's emotion becomes today's fuel — the plan stays cold.
Having an exit in the works made it easier to breathe.

choices.text: Take a half-day. Need to stop.  (self-care / reputation risk)
choices.result_text:
Took a half-day. Stayed home and didn't go anywhere.
Just that. And it was enough — more than expected.

title: The Manager Left
description:
Sudden.
The manager who had looked out for {name} — on the restructuring list.
Packed up quietly on the last day.
"You've got what it takes. Good luck." And gone.

When the people you lean on disappear — the organization looks different.

choices.text: Adapt to the new manager.  (adjustment / ego)
choices.result_text:
{name} started over under the new manager.
Took time. Different style.
Managed.

choices.text: Could be my turn next — time to move.  (vigilance / action)
choices.result_text:
{name} updated the résumé.
If good people get cut like this — the plan comes first.

title: Again
description:
It happened again.
Different meeting, different report.
{name}'s idea in the manager's mouth, delivered to senior leadership.

First time: swallowed it.
Second time — staying quiet is also a choice.

choices.text: File a formal complaint. Put it on record.  (self-respect / confrontation)
choices.result_text:
{name} submitted the situation to HR in writing.
The organization got uncomfortable. But the record existed.
The name won't be erased from the next one.

choices.text: Hand in the resignation.  (exit / career gap)
choices.result_text:
{name} submitted the resignation.
Manager said, "Why so suddenly?"
{name} knew the answer — and so did the manager.
